name: Field
hint: Press Create workspace with the fields empty, then fix them one by one: each entry strikes through and folds away.
description: Label, hint and error for any control, wired for screen readers, plus the parts around it: Fieldset groups fields under a legend with one error and one disabled switch, Label stands alone, and ErrorSummary lists a form's problems at the top after a failed submit. Each summary link scrolls to its field, focuses it and points at it with a ring; a fixed problem is struck through, ticks and folds away while the count rolls down.
intents: label and error message for a custom input
error summary at the top of a form
group form fields with a legend
wrap a third-party input with a label and hint
list of form errors that link to each field
fieldset to disable a group of inputs
usage: Use Field around a control the kit does not draw itself (your own <input>, a native <select>, a third-party date picker, a contenteditable box, a custom slider) so it gets the same label, hint, error line and required mark as Text Field beside it. Give it `label`, `hint` and `error` (a string you already have), and pass the control as a function child `{(p) => <input {...p} />}` or as one element (Field adds id, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby, aria-invalid, aria-required, disabled and readOnly to it, keeping any you set and extending your aria-describedby). A custom control deeper inside calls useField() for the same values. Field is for controls without a label of their own: Text Field, Select, Textarea and the other kit fields already draw label, hint and error, so use their own props instead (a kit field that has its own `label` inside a Field keeps it and Field does not add a second). `layout="row"` puts label and hint on the left for settings pages; it stacks below 440px of its own width. Bump `revealErrors` on every submit so a repeated error shakes again. Use Fieldset to group related fields under a `legend` ("Delivery address"), with one group `error` and `disabled` for everything inside; Radio Group and Checkbox Group are fieldsets already, so name them with their own `label` and only put them in a Fieldset that also holds other fields. Use ErrorSummary at the top of the form: keep it mounted, pass `errors` as [{ field: inputId, message }] (or `name` instead of `field`), and it opens on a failed submit, takes focus, links to each field and folds away entries as they are fixed. For a single message that is not about fields use Alert Banner.

keyboard.does: Moves to the control inside the Field; Field adds no stop of its own, and an open ErrorSummary's links come first.
Scrolls to that entry's field, moves focus into it and points at it with a ring.

screenReader: Field names its control with a real label (also aria-labelledby) and links `hint` or `error` with aria-describedby; `error` sets aria-invalid and is read in a live region, and `required` sets aria-required. Fieldset is a fieldset named by its `legend`. ErrorSummary is an alert labelled by its `title` that takes focus when errors arrive; each entry is a link to its field, and fixed entries are hidden from screen readers as they fold away.

exports.description: A real <fieldset> and <legend> for a group of fields. The legend lays out like a heading (15px / 620), with an optional description and one error for the group (an assertive live region; its space opens on a spring and the line shakes when it arrives). `disabled` is the native attribute, so every native control inside is disabled, kit fields included; Fields and useField() controls inside hear it too, and the contents dim once. Radio Group and Checkbox Group are fieldsets themselves: name one with its own `label`, and put it in a Fieldset only alongside other fields (a nested fieldset is announced with both legends). With `id`, the legend's id is `${id}-legend` (for aria-labelledby on an inner group that has no label of its own). The ref goes to the <fieldset>.

exports.example:
<Fieldset legend="Delivery address" description="We only ship within the EU." layout="grid" columns={2} error={addressError}>
  <Field label="Street" error={errors.street} style={{ gridColumn: "span 2" }}>{(p) => <input {...p} name="street" autoComplete="address-line1" />}</Field>
  <Field label="Postcode" error={errors.postcode}>{(p) => <input {...p} name="postcode" autoComplete="postal-code" />}</Field>
  <Field label="City" error={errors.city}>{(p) => <input {...p} name="city" autoComplete="address-level2" />}</Field>
</Fieldset>

exports.description: The block at the top of a form after a failed submit. Errors arrive as one block that grows open on a height spring, entries settling in on a short stagger; it is role="alert" with tabIndex -1 and takes focus when errors arrive (focusOnShow) and again on a resubmit (revealErrors, when it also shakes). Each entry is a link: it scrolls its field into view below `scrollMargin`, focuses it, and points at it with a ring in the danger tone that grows from the field's edge and fades (drawn on a fixed overlay that tracks the field; the field's own styles are not touched). When a field is fixed its entry is struck through, ticks and folds away while the entries below close the gap and the count rolls down; when the last one goes the block folds shut and focus inside it goes back where it came from. Entries are keyed by id, field or name, so a changed message updates in place. With no errors it renders nothing and takes no space (a flex parent's gap opens and closes with it). Reduced motion: entries appear and disappear in place, no stagger, strike or rolling count, and a still ring for a moment. Keep it mounted and pass []; mounted with errors already present it shows them at rest and takes focus.

exports.description: Hook for a custom control anywhere inside a Field: returns { id, "aria-labelledby", "aria-describedby", "aria-invalid", "aria-required", disabled, readOnly }, the same values a function child receives. Inside a Fieldset but no Field it returns disabled from the group (and the rest undefined), so a custom control can follow a disabled Fieldset.
